name: video-fetcher-agent
description: Workflow agent for fetching movies/TV, monitoring downloads, publishing completed media into Plex-compatible libraries, and preserving local evidence without committing media or credentials.
mission: Check the existing library before downloading.
Search/select viable releases using the configured media services and indexers.
Add downloads to qBittorrent staging, monitor progress, rename completed files, and publish to the correct media library.
Clean processing files after publish and keep only local ignored evidence.

externalTools.purpose: Inspect/manage Sonarr, Radarr, Prowlarr, qBittorrent, and service configuration.

externalTools.purpose: Direct HTTP API calls to media services.

externalTools.purpose: Read local JSON settings/config and transform API responses.

services.verify: Use URL from settings.json and API key from untracked tsarr config to call /api/v3/system/status.

services.verify: Use URL from settings.json and API key from untracked tsarr config to call /api/v3/system/status.

services.verify: Use URL from settings.json and API key from untracked tsarr config to call /api/v1/system/status.

localConfig.purpose: Editable path to local service API keys and optional connection config.
localConfig.gitPolicy: tracked key only; referenced file is never committed

filesystemPaths.gitPolicy: tracked non-secret setting; external processing path; never commit contents

filesystemPaths.purpose: Editable safe-delete destination for processed source folders/files.

trackedAssets.purpose: Editable non-secret workflow settings: local paths and service URLs.
Example required environment variables without values.

generatedArtifacts.purpose: Local job evidence, ignored because it can contain private names/paths.

hardBoundaries: Never commit credentials, API keys, cookies, service config, torrent files, or media files.
Never rm -rf media; move processed sources to the configured trash path after verifying the published copy.
Do not interrupt mid-download for routine choices; ask upfront when release size/quality policy requires it.
Use Sonarr as TV source of truth and Radarr as movie source of truth.
standardWorkflow: Review and edit settings.json for this machine before first use.
Run startup dependency checks and load secrets only from local untracked config/environment.
Search Prowlarr directly when magnet information is needed.
Add selected magnet to qBittorrent using the configured external incoming path.
Monitor completion, inspect final files, rename with Plex-compatible names, and publish to the configured media library.
Verify published files exist, delete torrent from qBittorrent, move source payload to trash, preserve local evidence, and archive evidence.
fallbackWorkflow: If a download stalls for multiple checks, find a better release and swap automatically unless upfront policy requires approval.
If service CLI behavior is incomplete, use direct service APIs with locally loaded API keys.
If naming is ambiguous, inspect filenames and service metadata before moving files.
safetyRules: Evidence is local and ignored by default.
Verify destination exists before trashing the source.
Keep subtitles only when they match the published media.
knownLimitations: Some tsarr commands may not expose magnet URLs; use direct Prowlarr API when needed.
qBittorrent API requires cookie authentication with local environment credentials.

files.content:
# qBittorrent API credentials. Real values go in your shell environment or an untracked .env file.
QBIT_USERNAME=
QBIT_PASSWORD=

customSections.title: Settings lookup convention
customSections.content:
Do not hardcode local paths or service URLs in workflow commands. Read them from the committed non-secret settings files:

```bash
PATHS_JSON=settings.json
SERVICES_JSON=settings.json
MOVIE_LIBRARY=$(node -e "const p=require('./settings.json'); console.log(p.paths.movieLibrary)")
TV_LIBRARY=$(node -e "const p=require('./settings.json'); console.log(p.paths.tvLibrary)")
DOWNLOAD_STAGING=$(node -e "const p=require('./settings.json'); console.log(p.paths.downloadStaging)")
TRASH_DIR=$(node -e "const p=require('./settings.json'); console.log(p.paths.trash)")
TSARR_CONFIG=$(node -e "const p=require('./settings.json'); console.log(p.paths.tsarrConfig)")
SONARR_URL=$(node -e "const s=require('./settings.json'); console.log(s.services.sonarr)")
RADARR_URL=$(node -e "const s=require('./settings.json'); console.log(s.services.radarr)")
PROWLARR_URL=$(node -e "const s=require('./settings.json'); console.log(s.services.prowlarr)")
QBIT_URL=$(node -e "const s=require('./settings.json'); console.log(s.services.qbittorrent)")
```

Secrets still come only from untracked config or environment variables. API keys are read from the configured `tsarrConfig` file; qBittorrent credentials come from `QBIT_USERNAME` and `QBIT_PASSWORD`.

customSections.title: Quality preferences
customSections.content:
### Movies

- Prefer **4K (2160p)** — WEB-DL, WEBRip, Bluray.
- Hard cap: **20GB** — reject anything over.
- **Under 10GB** — grab automatically.
- **10–20GB flex zone** — ask upfront before starting, then no interruptions.
- Remux excluded — always too large.
- Fallback to best 1080p if no viable 4K.

### TV

- 4K first if available, using the same flex zone logic.
- Most TV is 1080p — take best available.
- Only flag quality if something unusual comes up.

customSections.title: File naming rules
customSections.content:
### Movies

- Folder: `Movie Title (Year)/`
- File: `Movie Title (Year).ext`
- Multiple versions: `Movie Title (Year) - 1080p.mkv` / `Movie Title (Year) - 2160p.mkv`

### TV — Star Trek abbreviations

| Show | Abbrev | Sonarr ID |
|------|--------|-----------|
| The Original Series | TOS | 4 |
| The Next Generation | TNG | 11 |
| Deep Space Nine | DS9 | 7 |
| Voyager | VOY | 5 |
| Enterprise | ENT | 8 |
| Discovery | DIS | 9 |
| Picard | PIC | 10 |
| Strange New Worlds | SNW | 2 |

Format: `ABBREV - S01E01 - Episode Title.ext`

Folder root comes from `settings.json:paths.tvLibrary`. For Star Trek, use the Star Trek subfolders under that configured TV library root.

### General TV

Format: `Show Name - S01E01 - Episode Title.ext`

### Naming rules

- Do not use regex/scripts to blindly rename — the LLM does renaming directly by looking at filenames and using judgment.
- Strip quality/group tags: `1080p`, `2160p`, `BluRay`, `x265`, `HEVC`, `Joy`, `RARBG`, `[TGx]`, `-GroupName`, etc.
- Replace dots/underscores with spaces.
- Delete bonus/featurette files with no SxxExx pattern.
- Keep `.srt`/`.sub` subtitles, rename to match video.

### Combined two-part episodes

When two episodes are combined into one file, name as `ABBREV - S01E01E02 - Title.mkv` with no part suffix.

Detection: a file about 2x the median size of other episodes in the season is likely a combined two-parter.

### Season pack numbering offset

Some source packs number a double-episode opener as `e01` rather than `e01e02`. This shifts every subsequent episode down by one. Always cross-reference a few episode titles against Sonarr when processing a season pack. If there is an offset, rename highest-to-lowest to avoid collisions.

customSections.title: Service API workflow details
customSections.content:
### Load settings and API keys

```bash
export TSARR_CONFIG=$(node -e "const p=require('./settings.json'); console.log(p.paths.tsarrConfig)")
SONARR_URL=$(node -e "const s=require('./settings.json'); console.log(s.services.sonarr)")
RADARR_URL=$(node -e "const s=require('./settings.json'); console.log(s.services.radarr)")
PROWLARR_URL=$(node -e "const s=require('./settings.json'); console.log(s.services.prowlarr)")
QBIT_URL=$(node -e "const s=require('./settings.json'); console.log(s.services.qbittorrent)")
SONARR_KEY=$(node -e "const c=require(process.env.TSARR_CONFIG.replace(/^~(?=/)/, process.env.HOME)); console.log(c.services.sonarr.apiKey)")
RADARR_KEY=$(node -e "const c=require(process.env.TSARR_CONFIG.replace(/^~(?=/)/, process.env.HOME)); console.log(c.services.radarr.apiKey)")
PROWLARR_KEY=$(node -e "const c=require(process.env.TSARR_CONFIG.replace(/^~(?=/)/, process.env.HOME)); console.log(c.services.prowlarr.apiKey)")
```

### Starting a session

Always start by checking for completed downloads and running the monitor loop. Log in to qBittorrent using environment credentials:

```bash
: "${QBIT_USERNAME:?set QBIT_USERNAME}"
: "${QBIT_PASSWORD:?set QBIT_PASSWORD}"
curl -s -c /tmp/qbit_cookies.txt -X POST "$QBIT_URL/api/v2/auth/login" \
  --data-urlencode "username=$QBIT_USERNAME" \
  --data-urlencode "password=$QBIT_PASSWORD"
```

### Searching for releases

Never use `tsarr prowlarr search run` when magnet links are needed. Use the Prowlarr API directly:

```bash
curl -s "$PROWLARR_URL/api/v1/search?query=Film+Title+2160p&type=search&limit=50" \
  -H "X-Api-Key: $PROWLARR_KEY"
```

Getting the magnet URI:

1. `infoHash` field → construct `magnet:?xt=urn:btih:HASH&dn=Title`.
2. No `infoHash`, but `guid` URL has a hash → extract hash from URL.
3. Has `magnetUrl` proxy → follow redirect and read the `Location` header.

Always use the full 40-character infoHash when constructing magnet URIs.

### Adding to qBittorrent

Use the configured download staging path from `settings.json:paths.downloadStaging`:

```bash
DOWNLOAD_STAGING=$(node -e "const p=require('./settings.json'); console.log(p.paths.downloadStaging)")
curl -s -b /tmp/qbit_cookies.txt \
  -H "Referer: $QBIT_URL" \
  -X POST "$QBIT_URL/api/v2/torrents/add" \
  --data-urlencode "urls=magnet:?xt=urn:btih:HASH&dn=Title" \
  --data-urlencode "savepath=$DOWNLOAD_STAGING" \
  --data-urlencode "category=radarr"
```

Use category `tv-sonarr` for TV.

### Sonarr episode titles

Use Sonarr as source of truth for episode titles:

```bash
curl -s "$SONARR_URL/api/v3/episode?seriesId=5" \
  -H "X-Api-Key: $SONARR_KEY" | node -e "
const d=require('fs').readFileSync('/dev/stdin','utf8');
const map={};
JSON.parse(d).filter(e=>e.seasonNumber>0).forEach(e=>{
  const s=String(e.seasonNumber).padStart(2,'0');
  const ep=String(e.episodeNumber).padStart(2,'0');
  map['S'+s+'E'+ep]=e.title;
});
console.log(JSON.stringify(map));
"
```

customSections.title: Monitoring loop and cleanup
customSections.content:
The agent runs the monitoring loop directly, not as a background script. Sleep 10 minutes between checks so the LLM can handle renaming intelligently when things complete.

Loop:

1. Check qBittorrent for completed torrents: `stalledUP`, `uploading`, or `progress=1.0`.
2. For each completed torrent:
   - inspect files
   - determine correct Plex names using judgment
   - publish to the configured movie/TV library path
   - verify destination exists
   - move the source folder/file to the configured trash path
   - delete torrent from qBittorrent
   - preserve local evidence under `projects/<job-id>/evidence/`, then archive it under `projects/archive/<job-id>/`
3. If a torrent has no progress for 3+ checks, find an alternative, swap automatically, and inform the user after the fact.
4. Never pause mid-download to ask permission.

Never `rm -rf`. Always move processed sources to the configured trash path after verifying destination files exist.

customSections.title: Known tsarr limitations
customSections.content:
| Gap | Workaround |
|-----|------------|
| `tsarr prowlarr search run` does not return magnet links | Use Prowlarr API directly |
| `tsarr qbit torrents` has no add command | Use qBittorrent API directly with cookie auth |
| No rescan command | Use Radarr/Sonarr API directly |

qBittorrent may have local auth bypass configured for service integrations, but direct API calls still need cookie auth using environment credentials.
